section_summary: This section closes a Textile Mission report on Japanese cotton mills, then records requests for the report and correspondence about publishing and distributing it. It includes a detailed address on Japan’s rayon industry, discussions of textile exports to the Philippines, India and Siam, and consular despatches enclosing press reports on cotton, rayon and silk production.

subfiles.title: Textile Mission report: cotton mill requirements
subfiles.about: The mission assesses sizing materials, labor, power, coal, transport and storage for revived cotton production.
subfiles.summary: Corn starch, zinc chloride and other inputs are needed to process imported cotton. Food shortages hinder labor recruitment, though the mission considers a smaller workforce sufficient for available machinery. It judges power, coal, transport and warehouse capacity broadly adequate.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on addressee for Philippine letter
subfiles.about: Asks whether a draft letter should be addressed to General Romulo after his departure.
subfiles.summary: Queries the addressee; a note suggests Leonides S. Virata.

subfiles.title: Request for draft reply
subfiles.about: Requests that the International Resources Division draft a reply.
subfiles.summary: Asks IR to draft the reply.

subfiles.title: Philippine request for Japanese textiles
subfiles.about: Requests a Philippine share of Japanese textiles being considered for export.
subfiles.summary: Romulo says clothing is an urgent Philippine need and asks that its requirements be considered in Combined Textile Board allocations.

subfiles.title: Confidential copy of Textile Mission report
subfiles.about: Transmits the mission report while cautioning that it has not yet been cleared for public release.
subfiles.summary: Sends Yang a copy and asks him to treat it as confidential pending SCAP approval.

subfiles.title: Handwritten report classification note
subfiles.about: Comments on the report’s classification.
subfiles.summary: Brief, partly illegible note concerning classification.

subfiles.title: Senator Andrews requests mission report
subfiles.about: Requests a typewritten copy of the Textile Mission’s Japanese industry report.
subfiles.summary: The senator asks for the cotton, rayon and silk findings because printed copies are unavailable.

subfiles.title: Reply on availability of mission report
subfiles.about: Explains that copies are being reproduced after SCAP cleared the report for general distribution.
subfiles.summary: Promises a copy once additional printing is complete.

subfiles.title: Hayes G. Shimp inquiry to State Department
subfiles.from: M. P. Nock, Hayes G. Shimp, Inc.
subfiles.to: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Seeks rules for trading Japanese textiles with India.
subfiles.summary: Forwards an earlier Commerce Department inquiry and asks for definite procedures and trade policy.

subfiles.title: Enclosed inquiry on India–Japan textile trade
subfiles.to: U.S. Department of Commerce, Foreign Trade Bureau
subfiles.about: Asks how Indian importers can buy Japanese cotton and silk goods.
subfiles.summary: Offers sterling, rupees, dollars or cotton barter and asks about the purchasing channel.

subfiles.title: Commerce Department correspondence fragment
subfiles.about: A fragment of Commerce correspondence concerning the firm’s trade inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Only the closing and identification of Clark Byse remain legible.

subfiles.title: State Department reply fragment to Hayes G. Shimp
subfiles.from: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Appears to answer the firm’s inquiry about textile trade.
subfiles.summary: The substantive text is illegible; closing and drafting date survive.

subfiles.title: Reply fragment to American Viscose
subfiles.from: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.to: Jack C. Green, American Viscose Corporation
subfiles.about: A damaged draft reply to American Viscose correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Recipient and opening are visible, but the response is illegible.

subfiles.title: Siamese purchase of Japanese textiles
subfiles.about: Records discussion of a proposed Siamese purchase of Japanese textiles.
subfiles.summary: British officials offer to procure about 20 million yards for Siam but reject sterling payment. The State Department awaits further information before answering.

subfiles.title: Textile Research Institute publication proposal
subfiles.about: Offers to publish and distribute the Textile Mission report to industry.
subfiles.summary: Jacobs asks for permission and a copy while coordinating with Textile World over possible publication.

subfiles.title: Reply to publication proposal
subfiles.about: States that SCAP permits public publication and describes the State Department’s larger print run.
subfiles.summary: Whitman reports that 500 copies are being printed and forwards two copies to Jacobs.

subfiles.title: Press release on Textile Mission findings
subfiles.about: Summarizes mission findings on Japanese cotton, rayon, wool, machinery and labor.
subfiles.summary: The release lists mission members and observers, estimates reduced cotton and rayon capacity, reviews textile stocks and possible exports, and highlights machinery and food related labor constraints.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Wickliffe Rose’s address
subfiles.about: Forwards a copy of Rose’s address on Japan’s rayon industry.
subfiles.summary: Morton sends the address at Rose’s request.

subfiles.title: The Rayon Industry of Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Rose’s observations from the Textile Mission’s rayon survey.
subfiles.summary: Rose describes the mission’s personnel, travel, fieldwork and methods for estimating Japan’s remaining rayon capacity. He reviews plant machinery, production processes, raw material shortages, quality testing and research, including work at Yokohama and Kyoto. He argues that future output depends on supplies and markets and closes with observations on the occupation.

subfiles.title: Reply to Rebecca Morton
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Morton’s transmittal of Rose’s address.
subfiles.summary: The body is largely illegible; the reply refers to his address.

subfiles.title: Records routing slip
subfiles.about: Routes copies of a records item among State Department offices.
subfiles.summary: Lists action office and copy distribution.

subfiles.title: Return request
subfiles.about: Asks that the item be returned to Feinstein.
subfiles.summary: Brief return instruction.

subfiles.title: Article on rayon industry in Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards an article on Japan’s reduced rayon capacity and raw material needs.
subfiles.summary: The despatch highlights wartime machinery scrapping, limited current production and projected recovery, forwarding the article for the Department’s information.

subfiles.title: Rayon industry in Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese rayon capacity, production forecasts and material requirements.
subfiles.summary: Provides mill capacity figures and identifies coal, pulp, caustic soda and other shortages.

subfiles.title: Report copy transmittal
subfiles.about: Forwards two requested copies of the Textile Mission report.
subfiles.summary: The damaged draft records a two copy transmittal.

subfiles.title: Damaged reply concerning report
subfiles.about: A reply concerning the Textile Mission report.
subfiles.summary: The body is illegible.

subfiles.title: Pepperell request for mission report
subfiles.about: Requests the full Textile Mission report and asks whether there is a charge.
subfiles.summary: Parsons seeks a copy for Pepperell Manufacturing Company.

subfiles.title: Reply to Brackett Parsons
subfiles.about: Sends the requested Textile Mission report.
subfiles.summary: Whitman forwards a free copy.

subfiles.title: Combined Textile Committee urges Japanese exports
subfiles.about: Urges action on exporting Japanese cotton cloth allocated for Far Eastern countries.
subfiles.summary: The Committee fears that 120 million yards earmarked for second quarter export may be absorbed by Japanese domestic use. Rose asks for firm disposition of stocks and faster purchasing and shipment arrangements, noting a proposal for a Far Eastern purchasing mission.

subfiles.title: File copy of Committee correspondence
subfiles.about: Administrative markings refer to the Combined Textile Committee letter.
subfiles.summary: No substantive correspondence is legible.

subfiles.title: Report sent to Senator Eastland
subfiles.about: Sends the cleared Textile Mission report requested by Eastland.
subfiles.summary: Confirms the report is available and encloses it.

subfiles.title: Inquiry about Stanley Nehmer’s footlocker
subfiles.to: United States Political Adviser to SCAP, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Requests the disposition of Stanley Nehmer’s footlocker.
subfiles.summary: Asks Tokyo to report what happened to the footlocker.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of mission report
subfiles.about: Thanks Vincent for sending the Textile Mission press release and report.
subfiles.summary: Interchemical Corporation is analyzing the report.

subfiles.title: Report copies for Department of Agriculture
subfiles.about: Forwards two copies of the Textile Mission report.
subfiles.summary: Sends the requested copies.

subfiles.title: Report copies for Textile Section
subfiles.from: Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs
subfiles.about: Sends two copies of the report requested by telephone.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the two requested copies.

subfiles.title: Textile Research Institute renews publication offer
subfiles.about: Offers to publish the mission report if government printing will not provide broad distribution.
subfiles.summary: Jacobs proposes low cost industry distribution and asks to inspect the report first.

subfiles.title: Reply on government report distribution
subfiles.about: Describes intended government distribution of the mission report.
subfiles.summary: The damaged reply lists agencies, libraries, editors and technical readers among recipients.

subfiles.title: Harvard Baker Library requests textile reports
subfiles.about: Requests the Japan Textile Mission report and future reports on British India and China.
subfiles.summary: Cole asks for a released or confidential library copy and placement on the distribution list.

subfiles.title: Reply to Harvard Baker Library
subfiles.about: Forwards the Japan report and comments on the related India study.
subfiles.summary: Sends a copy and says Fred Taylor is working on a similar study in British India.

subfiles.title: Replacement record copy notice
subfiles.about: Designates an attached white telegram copy as the official record copy.
subfiles.summary: Instructs return of the replacement copy for filing.

subfiles.title: Telegram concerning Bunce’s proposed U.S. trip
subfiles.about: Relays approval of Bunce’s proposed U.S. trip and congratulations on an interim program.
subfiles.summary: Martin reacts favorably to Bunce’s travel and notes program approval.

subfiles.title: Articles on Japanese cotton and rayon situation
subfiles.about: Forwards two Times of India articles on Japanese textile production.
subfiles.summary: Donovan summarizes cotton shipment grades, weaving equipment shortages, rayon export planning, four shift mill operations and hosiery capacity. He asks whether the Department wants such articles forwarded regularly.

subfiles.title: Japan experiment in textile mills
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese mill experiment with four shifts and efforts to increase textile output.
subfiles.summary: Describes the shift experiment and production measures; much text is obscured.

subfiles.title: Short staple cotton for Japan and rayon exports plan
subfiles.about: Reports grades of U.S. cotton shipments and Japanese plans for cotton and rayon output.
subfiles.summary: Discusses short staple cotton, weavers’ equipment shortages, planned cloth exports and rayon industry standards and organization.

subfiles.title: Japanese silk exports
subfiles.about: Forwards an article on Japan’s proposed five year silk program.
subfiles.summary: Donovan summarizes projected mulberry acreage, raw silk production and exports, including possible Hokkaido sericulture.

subfiles.title: Aims of five year silk program
subfiles.about: Details Japanese mulberry planting, cocoon production and raw silk export targets.
subfiles.summary: Presents forecasts through 1950, discusses fertilizer and food constraints, and reports shipments to the United States.

subfiles.title: Draper Corporation requests mission report
subfiles.about: Requests a copy of the Textile Mission report.
subfiles.summary: Offers to pay any charge for a copy.

subfiles.title: Reply to Consul General Donovan
subfiles.about: Responds to Donovan’s inquiry about forwarding textile articles.
subfiles.summary: Most of the response is illegible.

subfiles.title: Routing slip for Bombay despatch 2902
subfiles.about: Routes Bombay despatch 2902 to State Department offices.
subfiles.summary: Lists action and copy recipients.

subfiles.title: Production of rayon yarn in Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards a Times of India report on Japanese rayon yarn output and input shortages.
subfiles.summary: Donovan reports that April yarn output doubled February’s but remained far below capacity. Wood pulp and caustic soda shortages threaten continued recovery; he again asks whether to keep sending articles.

subfiles.title: Production of rayon yarn
subfiles.about: Reports April rayon yarn production and compares March and April industry statistics.
subfiles.summary: Attributes increased output to coal deliveries but warns of depleted pulp and caustic soda stocks.

subfiles.title: Decline in Japanese cloth production
subfiles.about: Forwards an article on declining Japanese cotton yarn and cloth production.
subfiles.summary: Donovan describes exhausted cotton stocks, delayed U.S. imports, shifts toward rayon staple and low use of operable spindles.

subfiles.title: Cotton shortage in Japan
subfiles.about: Reports a fall in Japanese cotton yarn and cloth output.
subfiles.summary: Delayed American cotton shipments and dwindling mill stocks reduced output despite repaired spindle capacity.

subfiles.title: Consular despatch on Japanese textile production
subfiles.about: Forwards a Bombay Times of India article on planned textile production and coal supply.
subfiles.summary: Donovan cites projected increases in cotton and rayon yarn output and warns that coal shortages threaten the plans; the despatch continues beyond this section.
